title: What Zero-Latency Cloud Processing Is
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Zero-latency cloud processing is the pursuit of cloud computing that feels instantaneous: ultra-edge placement, predictive pre-computation, and protocol breakthroughs that hide round-trip delays so remote compute responds like local hardware. This record is the entry point of the teaching ladder for Zero-Latency Cloud Processing: start here, then move through the research state, the specifications, the public developments, the open challenges, and finally each piece needed to build it.
key_points: Zero-Latency Cloud Processing in one line: Zero-latency cloud processing is the pursuit of cloud computing that feels instantaneous: ultra-edge placement, predictive pre-computation, and protocol breakthroughs that hide round-trip delays so remote compute responds like local hardware.
Why it matters: Latency is the last barrier to moving everything to the cloud — kill it and any device becomes infinitely powerful..
Where it is used: cloud gaming, remote workstations, AR/VR streaming, real-time collaboration, autonomous systems..
Ladder rank 1 — the foundation. Everything else builds on this.

t: Current Research State of Zero-Latency Cloud Processing
title: Current Research State of Zero-Latency Cloud Processing
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Edge computing pushed compute to cell towers and central offices; 5G URLLC targets 1ms radio latency; and predictive techniques (speculative execution, foveated streaming) mask remaining delays. Research focuses on sub-millisecond networking, deterministic latency, and moving compute to within single-digit milliseconds of every user. Research moves in three waves: laboratory proof of concept, scaled prototypes under controlled conditions, and field trials. Zero-Latency Cloud Processing currently sits at the stage described above, and the pieces records show what each wave still needs.
